Appendix 2 Table of amendments: '28 March 2025 | Version 5 | Major Amendment' (Package A flood hazard overlay; Package B rezoning/Yaamba Road tables; Package C lot sizes and dual occupancy/multiple dwelling density in LDR/LMDR). ePlan revision API (api/l/vpr) lists a single revision: revisionId 49, revisionNotes 'Version 5', planOperative 03/28/2025, revisionDate 08/04/2025, revStatus 'Current'; rev TOC (api/l/rev/49/22-Oct-2026/1) shows planChanges = [] (no pending amendments). A web search found a 2026 LGIP/major amendment consultation (Jan-Feb 2026) but no evidence it has commenced; the ePlan still shows Version 5 as current at 22 Oct 2026. QHC: no reference to the 'Queensland Housing Code' anywhere in the retrieved scheme text (219 sections keyword-searched); Version 5 predates the QHC, and Part 1 still refers to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2. QHC adoption status: not adopted in the scheme text.

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Part 1 s1.6 (Building work regulated under the planning scheme) Table 1.6.1 names the Low density residential zone code, Low-medium density residential zone code and Character overlay code as 'Alternative provisions to the QDC MP1.1 and QDC MP1.2 for a class 1 and 10 building or structure' (Sections 32(b), 32(c) and 33 BA and section 10 BR). However, s5.6 states building work categories are 'Not applicable' and a dwelling house is 'Accepted' with assessment benchmarks 'Not applicable' in the LDR, LMDR, HDR, Township and Rural residential zones, so in practice the LDR/LMDR setbacks reach only dual occupancies (accepted subject to requirements) and assessable development; a dwelling house and its outbuildings in those zones default to the QDC. The Character overlay code AO8.1.1 is the only alternative provision that reaches dwelling-house outbuildings (garages, carports, enclosed outbuildings) directly, in the Residential character design control area. Rural (20 m all boundaries; Alton Downs precinct 6 m front) and Emerging community (6 m side/rear) zone setbacks apply to dwelling houses as accepted development requirements but those codes are not listed in Table 1.6.1. No Queensland Housing Code reference was found.

quotes.text:
- This planning scheme, through Part 5 (Tables of assessment), regulates building work in accordance with sections 32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975.
Editor’s note—The Building Act 1975 permits planning schemes to:
-
regulate, for the Building Code of Australia (BCA) or the Queensland Development Code (QDC), matters prescribed under a regulation under the Building Act 1975 (section 32). These include variations to provisions contained in parts MP1.1, MP1.2 and MP1.3 of the QDC such as heights of buildings related to obstruction and overshadowing, siting and design of buildings to provide visual privacy and adequate sight lines, on-site parking and outdoor living spaces. It may also regulate other matters, such as designating land liable to flooding, designating land as bushfire prone areas and transport noise corridors
-
deal with an aspect of, or matter related or incidental to building work prescribed under a regulation under section 32 of the Building Act 1975
-
specify alternative boundary clearances and site cover provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures under section 33 of the Building Act 1975.
Refer to Schedule 9 of the Regulation to determine assessable development, the type of assessment and any referrals applying to the building work.

definitions.text: For a building or structure, means the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot where the building or structure is.
A non-habitable class 10a building that is— - a shed, garage or carport; and - ancillary to a residential use carried out on the premises where the building is.

Dwelling house means a residential use of premises involving— - 1 dwelling for a single household and any domestic outbuildings associated with the dwelling; or - 1 dwelling for a single household, a secondary dwelling, and any domestic outbuildings associated with either dwelling.

The distance between a building or structure on premises and the boundary of the premises, measured from the part of the building or structure that is closest to the boundary, other than a part that is— - an architectural or ornamental attachment; or - a rainwater fitting.
Means a boundary of a lot which abuts a road.
